To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the PP2A scaffold and regulatory subunit expression is reduced in malignant prostate tissues and cell lines and this is responsible for its reduced function in prostate cancer cells.
PP2A scaffold and regulatory subunit loss is associated with prostate cancer progression, and that this loss is responsible for altered PP2A function and increased tumour aggressiveness.
loss of PP2A scaffold and regulatory subunit expression is responsible for its functional inactivation during PCa progression.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a new mechanism of PCa pathogenesis that can lead to the development of new therapeutic targets.
the identification and characterisation of the role of PP2A subunits in PCa, and the potential therapeutic targets for this malignancy.
the identification of PP2A subunit expression patterns in prostate tumorigenesis, which could be used as a prognostic biomarker for the diagnosis and treatment of PCa patients.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the expression of PP2A subunits is altered in PCa, and that PP2A is a potential target for the development of novel therapeutics.
PP2A is downregulated in PCa and that this downregulation is due to loss of expression of the regulatory and scaffold subunits of PP.
the expression levels of PP2Ac, PP2A-A, and PP2A-B′γ subunits are reduced in PCa, which may contribute to its progression.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
loss of PP2A subunits is responsible for the enhanced metastatic potential of AI PCa cells, which is mediated through the activation of the AKT pathway.
PP2A is a tumour suppressor and its loss contributes to PCa progression.
the loss of expression of PP2A scaffold and regulatory subunit is a key event in prostate cancer progression.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the expression pattern of PP2A subunits is differentially modulated during prostate cancer progression.
loss of PP2A expression is not a random phenomenon but is rather orchestrated to enhance the metastatic potential of PCa cells.
PP2A subunits may be potential therapeutic targets for PCa.
